newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ANDRUW JONES HOMERS TWICE AS BRAVES DEMOLISH YANKEES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ANDRUW JONES HOMERS TWICE AS BRAVES DEMOLISH YANKEES.

text.p: Nineteen-year-old Andruw Jones homered twice and drove in five runs while John Smoltz allowed just two hits in six innings as the Atlanta Braves demolished the New York Yankees 12-1 in the World Series opener Sunday.

In a Game 1 delayed one day by heavy rain and wind Saturday, Jones scored three times and had three hits and Smoltz threw no-hit ball through four innings in a show of complete domination by the National League champions.
Game 2 of the best-of-seven series is again in Yankee Stadium on Monday night.

Jones, who in just under two months this year jumped from the low minor leagues to the majors, hit full-count, two-out homers in the second and third innings, the first scoring two runs and the second one three.
In the second inning, one out after National League Championship series hero Javier Lopez poked a single up the middle, Jones smacked a 3-2 pitch 380 feet into the left-field seats to make it 2-0.
Jones became the youngest man ever to homer in the World Series at 19 years, 6 months, and the 25th to homer in his first Series at-bat.
The previous youngest was the Yankees' Mickey Mantle at 20 years, 11 months, in 1952. Mantle, the World Series all-time home run king with 18, would have turned 65 on this day.

In the third inning, Jeff Blauser led off with a line single to left and Marquis Grissom flared a single to centre. Mark Lemke bunted them to second and third and Chipper Jones singled through the shortstop hole, scoring both men and taking second on the throw. That made it 4-0.
Chipper Jones stole third on the first pitch to Fred McGriff, who drove him in with a single to centre.

After Lopez drew a walk and Jermaine Dye flied out with reliever Brian Boehringer now pitching, Andruw Jones fell behind 1-2, fouled off a couple, took the count to 3-2 and then slammed his second homer into the bullpen area beyond left field to make it 8-0.
Jones became the second man to homer in his first two World Series at-bats, after Gene Tenace of the Oakland Athletics in 1972.
During the regular season, Jones had already become the youngest National Leaguer to homer in 11 years, and the youngest major leaguer in 15 years to hit two homers in a game.
Jones this year jumped from A-Ball Durham to Double-A Greenville (June 19) to Triple-A Richmond (July 31) to the majors when he joined the Braves on August 14.
In the fifth, McGriff added a solo shot off the right-field foul pole to make it 9-0.
The Yanks finally scored in the bottom of the fifth when Derek Jeter walked and Wade Boggs got New York's first hit, doubling over Grissom's head in centre, scoring Jeter.

Andruw Jones led off the sixth with a ground ball to third along with a shard of his broken bat that hit Boggs in the leg, and Tino Martinez could not scoop the throw at first. Then Mariano Duncan fumbled Ryan Klesko's tailor-made double-play ball off his wrist, and men were on first and second.

After Blauser's fly-out advanced Jones to third, Grissom brought him home with a liner to left to make it 10-1. Lemke singled for another RBI and after David Weathers came on in relief, Chipper Jones hit a sacrifice fly to make it 12-1.

Smoltz, who walked five and struck out four, got the win while Andy Pettitte, who yielded six hits and seven runs in 2 1/3 innings, took the loss. Four Atlanta relievers allowed just two hits over the final three innings.
